name: CV / Resume Analysis - Game Development
description: Signals extracted from the user's CV/resume to evidence Game Development skills. CV data provides self-reported information that must be cross-validated with other sources.

extraction_rules.description: How to extract and weight information from CV content.

sections.description: Explicit list of technologies, engines, and tools mentioned in skills section.
sections.notes: Low strength because listing a skill doesn't prove proficiency. Must cross-reference with portfolio and projects.

sections.description: Job descriptions and responsibilities mentioning game development activities.
sections.notes: Higher strength when specific shipped titles, gameplay systems, or technical contributions are described.
quality_indicators: Shipped game titles with platform and studio details
Specific engine and language technologies mentioned in context
Quantifiable outcomes (optimized frame rate by X%, reduced load time by Y%)
Action verbs indicating hands-on work (implemented, architected, optimized, shipped)
Duration and recency of game development experience

sections.description: Personal game projects, game jam entries, or academic game development.
sections.notes: Higher strength if linked to itch.io, Steam, GitHub, or demo video. Game jam entries indicate practical ability under time pressure.
quality_indicators: Links to playable builds, source code, or demo videos
Game jam participation (Ludum Dare, GMTK, Global Game Jam)

sections.description: Relevant courses, degrees, and academic background in game development or computer science.
sections.notes: Game design/development degrees provide context. Computer science with graphics/game focus is relevant.

sections.description: Professional certifications related to game engines and development.
sections.notes: Certifications alone are NOT evidence of practical skill. They indicate theoretical knowledge and should be cross-validated.

signal_mapping.description: How CV mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Mentions Unity, Unreal, or Godot in work experience with specific activities
Lists game engine in skills section only
Describes implementing gameplay systems with C#, C++, or GDScript
Describes performance optimization with profiling and memory management
Describes rendering pipeline or shader development work
Has Unity Certified Programmer without project evidence
Describes custom tool or editor pipeline development
Describes physics simulation or collision system work
Shipped titles on consoles (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch)
Describes save system or data persistence implementation
Describes ECS or data-oriented design architecture
Describes custom shader or rendering pipeline development
Describes multiplayer or online game development
Describes optimizing game performance with quantifiable FPS improvements
CI/CD or build pipeline experience for game projects
Describes game balancing or economy design with data-driven approach
Describes behavior tree or AI system implementation for NPCs

important_notes: CV data is self-reported and inherently unreliable as standalone evidence
Always cross-validate CV claims with GitHub portfolio and LinkedIn data
Certifications should NEVER be the sole evidence for a skill rating
Look for specificity and depth — 'worked with Unity' is weaker than 'implemented ECS-based combat system in Unity DOTS reducing CPU time by 40%'
Shipped game titles carry significantly more weight than personal projects
Game jam participation indicates practical ability under time pressure
Recency matters — skills used 3+ years ago may not reflect current engine versions
